proposals.before: His grandson Sun Xingwu, a jinshi, rose to Vice Minister of Personnel.
proposals.after: His grandson Xingwu, a jinshi, rose to Vice Minister of Personnel.
proposals.reason: 孫 means grandson, not surname Sun; Xingwu is the given name.

proposals.before: His grandson Sun Xingwu, a jinshi, served as Vice Minister of Personnel.
proposals.after: His grandson Xingwu, a jinshi, served as Vice Minister of Personnel.
proposals.reason: 孫 means grandson, not surname Sun.

proposals.before: In year 27 Shandong Governor Zhang Qian was caught bringing silver to Beijing to bribe officials; when the case broke he was arrested, and the testimony implicated Gao Shiqi.
proposals.after: In year 27 Shandong Governor Zhang Gan was caught bringing silver to Beijing to bribe officials; when the case broke he was arrested, and the testimony implicated Gao Shiqi.
proposals.reason: Same person as 張汧 (Zhang Gan) named earlier.

proposals.before: Zhang Qian nursed groundless resentment and smeared me with innuendo; I could not have cleared my name but for the emperor's clear judgment, which thwarted the slander.
proposals.after: Zhang Gan nursed groundless resentment and smeared me with innuendo; I could not have cleared my name but for the emperor's clear judgment, which thwarted the slander.
proposals.reason: Same person as 張汧 (Zhang Gan) named earlier.

proposals.before: In time his followers multiplied; he founded a faction of his own. He bound Wang Hongxu to him as a die-hard ally, took He Kai, a supervising secretary, as a sworn brother, treated the Hanlin academician Chen Yuanlong as kinsman in a patron–nephew bond, and linked his children's marriages to Hongxu's elder brother Songling. All became his trusted agents, recruiting backers throughout the empire.
proposals.after: In time his followers multiplied; he founded a faction of his own. He bound Wang Hongxu to him as a die-hard ally, took He Kai, a supervising secretary, as a sworn brother, treated the Hanlin academician Chen Yuanlong as kinsman in a patron–nephew bond, and linked his children's marriages to Hongxu's elder brother Xuling. All became his trusted agents, recruiting backers throughout the empire.
proposals.reason: 頊齡 is Wang Xuling, not Songling.

proposals.before: In sum, Gao Shiqi, Wang Hongxu, Chen Yuanlong, He Kai, Wang Songling, and the rest have the nature of wolves, hearts of scorpions, and faces of ogres.
proposals.after: In sum, Gao Shiqi, Wang Hongxu, Chen Yuanlong, He Kai, Wang Xuling, and the rest have the nature of wolves, hearts of scorpions, and faces of ogres.
proposals.reason: 頊齡 is Wang Xuling, not Songling.

proposals.before: The historians observe: Scholar-officials who served directly in the inner court were called "study rooms," preserving the pre-conquest nomenclature.
proposals.after: The historians observe: When scholar-officials served on duty in the inner court, it was called the "Study," preserving the old name from before the conquest of the Pass.
proposals.reason: 谓之「书房」names the inner-court duty/institution, not the officials themselves as “study rooms.”

proposals.before: The historian comments: Confucian officials attending directly in the inner court are called "study rooms," preserving the old name from before entering the Pass.
proposals.after: The historian comments: Confucian officials attending directly in the inner court—[this service] is called the "Study," preserving the old name from before entering the Pass.
proposals.reason: Same referent error as idiomatic: 谓之 points to the post/service name 书房, not a label for the men.

proposals.before: The Southern Study with poetry, prose, calligraphy, and painting supplies the imperial—rank divided pure and urgent, participates in intimate counsel.
proposals.after: The Southern Study supplies poetry, prose, calligraphy, and painting for imperial use; its station is pure and close, and it takes part in confidential counsel.
proposals.reason: Literal English is garbled (“supplies the imperial—rank divided pure and urgent”) and obscures 地分清切 and 参与密勿.

proposals.before: At first seeing Shiqi obtain ancient men's poetry and prose, one glance and he knew their period; in the heart taking it strange—not long, I too could do it.
proposals.after: At first, seeing Shiqi take up ancient poetry and prose and know their period at a glance, I thought it strange in my heart; before long, I too could do it.
proposals.reason: 得古人诗文 means handling/reading the texts, not “obtain ancient men's poetry”; current literal is misleading and ungrammatical.

proposals.before: Yet they leaned on power, formed factions, accepted bribes, and pursued private gain, and were impeached again and again; the Kangxi Emperor bent the law to preserve them.
proposals.after: Yet they leaned on power, formed factions, accepted bribes, and pursued private gain, and were impeached again and again; the Kangxi Emperor leniently preserved them.
proposals.reason: 曲予保全 means the emperor accommodated/spared them; “bent the law” overstates a legal violation not stated in the Chinese.

decisions.reason: After Wang Hongxu's biography, s0170 孫興吾 uses 孫 as kinship 'grandson,' not a surname; Xingwu is the given name. Removing false surname Sun is required and the proposed sentence is accurate.
The literal field likewise misreads 孫 as surname Sun; the proposed 'His grandson Xingwu' correctly treats 孫 as kinship and 興吾 as the given name.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 孫興吾，進士，官吏部侍郎。

decisions.reason: The Chinese names 張汧; 汧 is read qiān, so Zhang Qian is the correct romanization. Changing Qian to Gan introduces a naming error rather than fixing one.
s0196 again has 張汧; original Zhang Qian correctly renders 汧 as qiān. The proposed Zhang Gan misromanizes the same graph.
s0210 names 鴻緒兄頊齡; 頊齡 is Xuling, not Songling. Replacing Songling with Xuling corrects the personal name while leaving the rest of the sentence intact.
s0232 lists 王頊齡 among the impeached clique; the original Wang Songling misreads 頊齡, and Wang Xuling restores the correct name.
In 儒臣直内廷，谓之「书房」, 谓之 names the duty/institution 书房, not the officials as 'study rooms.' The proposed idiomatic correctly makes the Study the referent and preserves 未入关前.

decisions.after: The historian comments: When Confucian officials attend directly in the inner court, it is called the "Study," preserving the old name from before entering the Pass.
decisions.reason: The original wrongly applies 「书房」 to the men; the proposal correctly retargets 谓之 to the service name but the bracketed '[this service]' is awkward editorial English. A clean clause with 'it is called the Study' fixes the referent without brackets.

The before literal garbles 供禦 and 地分淸切 into unintelligible English. The proposed rendering accurately gives imperial-use supply, a pure-and-close station, and participation in confidential counsel (參與密勿).

sourceWitness.excerpt: 南書房以詩文書畫供禦，地分淸切，參與密勿。

decisions.reason: 得古人詩文 means handling/reading ancient poetry and prose, not obtaining 'ancient men's' writings; the proposed literal is grammatical and matches the Chinese sense of 一覽即知其時代 and 心以爲異.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 初見士奇得古人詩文，一覽即知其時代，心以爲異

decisions.reason: 曲予保全 means the emperor accommodated or leniently spared them; 'bent the law' invents a legal breach not stated in the Chinese. 'Leniently preserved' is accurate and natural.
